title: CPU scheduling
summary: A scheduler chooses which ready process uses the CPU. Arrival time, burst length, policy and tie-breaking rules affect the timeline and the resulting wait, response and turnaround times.
claims: Turnaround is completion time minus arrival time.
Response is first CPU start minus arrival time.
Waiting is turnaround minus CPU burst for a CPU-only workload.

misconceptions.text: Response time and turnaround time always mean the same thing.

title: Round Robin
summary: Round Robin gives a running process at most one quantum before placing it at the back of the ready queue if it still has work. Arrivals and queue order therefore matter.
claims: A process that finishes before its quantum ends does not use the rest of that quantum.
Changing the quantum can change response and waiting times.

misconceptions.text: Every process joins the ready queue at time zero regardless of its arrival.
